## Why This Is Asked
This question evaluates your ability to influence without authority in high-stakes releases—a common scenario at fintech and social companies where Product, Engineering, and Compliance often have competing priorities. - What metrics did you track post-release to confirm the launch was successful?
- How would you handle this scenario if the compliance concern emerged after the initial launch?

I believed we should fix a critical bug affecting users, while my manager wanted to ship new features for a marketing deadline. I requested a one-on-one meeting to discuss my concerns calmly. I came prepared with data showing the bug was affecting 20% of our user base and causing churn. Rather than just stating my position, I asked for his perspective and listened first. We discovered he was under pressure from leadership about the launch. I acknowledged that constraint, then suggested a compromise: we could ship a lighter version of the new feature while addressing the bug in a hotfix within the same week. He agreed, and we delivered both on time. This experience taught me the importance of separate ego from the issue, coming with solutions rather than just objections, and finding common ground by understanding the other person's constraints. We ended up having a much stronger working relationship afterward.

## Why This Is Asked
Tests facilitation, equitable participation, and influence without authority. Focuses on beginner-friendly, real-world cross-functional collaboration.

## Key Concepts
- Facilitation techniques (round-robin, timeboxing)
- Inclusive collaboration (silent brainstorming)
- Ownership and accountability (lite RACI)
- Follow-up discipline and measurement

## Code Example
```javascript

const meetingNotes = [];
function addNote(domain, risk, owner) { meetingNotes.push({domain, risk, owner}); }
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you measure improvement over iterations?
- What would you do if a domain refuses ownership?
